ai.description: *Ophiomorus raithmai* is a slender, cylindrical skink reaching 15 cm. It is pale sandy-brown with dark lateral stripes and possesses three digits on each limb. Its snout is wedge-shaped for sand-swimming.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophiomorus raithmai* is best distinguished by its three digits per limb, whereas most other Indian *Ophiomorus* species possess four or five digits.
ai.habitat: *Ophiomorus raithmai* inhabits the arid, sandy desert regions of the Thar Desert, typically found in areas with sparse xerophytic vegetation and loose, shifting dunes.
ai.behavior: The Three-fingered Sand-fish is a specialized burrower that "swims" through loose desert sands to forage for small invertebrates while remaining concealed from predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophiomorus raithmai* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between July and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophiomorus raithmai* is endemic to the arid Thar Desert region of Rajasthan, India, typically inhabiting sandy substrates at low elevations.
